solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dude must not upset Nobel Peace Prize winner

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over, so the letters of the three words before it land in a new order

blocks.note: eleven letters of fodder, all used

explanation.surface: A warning to some casual fellow not to offend a famous laureate.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole phrase 'Dude must not' is the fodder; DESMOND TUTU was the South African archbishop who won the prize in 1984.
explanation.definitionFit: The archbishop received the 1984 award for his campaign against apartheid, so he is an example of such a laureate.

clue.text: Neglected detectives taken advantage of

blocks.note: DIs are detective inspectors
someone exploited has been used

explanation.surface: Officers who were ignored and then exploited by their superiors.
explanation.walkthrough: DI (Detective Inspector) is a standard crossword abbreviation, here plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abandoned and no longer in service has been left alone, a close synonym of an adjective meaning ignored.

clue.text: Figure in charge still

blocks.note: a stat is a statistic, a figure
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A statue in charge of things that never moves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb (yet) tacked on the end, but it is the adjective meaning motionless.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe an object not moving at all, an adjective synonym for being motionless.

clue.text: Eclipse Hades, or vow to be converted

indicators.note: converting something changes it into another form, so the letters of the underworld and the promise are remade

blocks.note: ten letters of fodder: the underworld, a conjunction and a promise

explanation.surface: A religious choice: outshine the underworld, or take a vow and join the faithful.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'converted' suggests religious conversion; here it only rearranges the letters of 'Hades, or vow'.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something in the shade by outshining it is a verb synonym for the transitive sense of eclipsing it.

clue.text: Entrance heartless doctor

indicators.note: without a heart means the central letters of the medical word are cut away

blocks.note: the physician in full; its middle pair then goes

explanation.surface: An unkind medic standing at the way in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' could be read as the verb to enchant, but here it is the noun, a way in; removing the CT at the centre leaves DOOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged panel you walk through to get into a room is the commonest way in, a straightforward noun synonym.

clue.text: Most extreme chapter leaves cult on island with couple

indicators.note: the chapter's abbreviation departs from the word for a sect, so it is struck out

blocks.note: the sect itself, before the chapter's letter goes
c is the abbreviation for chapter; this is the letter removed
I is the abbreviation for island
to couple animals is to mate them

explanation.surface: A tale of a cult branch walking out to settle on an island with a pair of followers.
explanation.walkthrough: CULT minus C gives ULT; 'couple' is a verb here, to mate, not a pair of people.
explanation.definitionFit: The furthest or final point of something is at its limit, so the adjective matches a superlative meaning greatest or last.

clue.text: Swedish city unfortunately starts to prevent protest, upsetting revolutionary

indicators.note: the beginnings of the three following words are all that is taken from them
a revolution turns something right round, so the whole assembled string runs backwards

blocks.note: alas is the exclamation for 'unfortunately'
the first letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A Swedish town trying to stop an upsetting demonstration by a radical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upsetting' looks like the reversal signal but only lends its first letter; 'revolutionary' is the real indicator, and it applies to the whole assembled string.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppsala is a university city north of Stockholm, so it is one example of a town in that Scandinavian country.

clue.text: Single man about to get married is boring in front of an audience

indicators.note: to bore is to drill into, so the man about to wed goes inside the word for single

blocks.note: one = single
a stag is a groom at his stag night, the British bachelor party

explanation.surface: A dull bachelor about to marry, droning on before a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' pretends to mean dull; it means drilling into ONE. A stag party is the British name for a groom's pre-wedding night out.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer standing on the boards in a theatre is being watched by spectators, so the adverb matches being seen performing.

clue.text: Not to be visited, like an exhausted kangaroo?

blocks.note: a place forbidden to enter
a kangaroo that is worn out has no leaps left in it

explanation.surface: A tired marsupial in a zone that is closed to visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the phrase literally: bounds are a kangaroo's leaps, and a spent animal has run out of them. The question mark flags the whimsy.
explanation.definitionFit: An area declared off limits is forbidden territory, and literally a jumper with no leaps left has used all its hops.

clue.text: In a way, this is army doctor ignoring limitations, knocking back drink

definitions.text: In a way, this is army

indicators.note: limitations are the edges of a word, so the medic's outer letters are dropped
knocking back a drink is gulping it, and 'back' also sends the word for drink in the other direction

blocks.note: the physician in full, before its first and last letters go
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: An army medic who disregards restrictions and downs a stiff drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Army doctor' wants to be MO, but 'army' belongs to the definition: an octopus is, playfully, 'army' because it is all arms.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea creature has eight tentacles, so a pun reads it as full of limbs in the jokey adjective sense.

clue.text: Horrible hag can smell coins

indicators.note: something horrible is a mess, so the letters of the phrase after it are jumbled

blocks.note: eleven letters of fodder

explanation.surface: A nasty old witch who can sniff out money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smell' reads as a verb in the surface but is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose metal pieces of low value in a pocket or purse are what the phrase names, a plural noun match.

clue.text: Try to get hold of sparkling wine, most delicious!

indicators.note: the word for try grabs the wine, so the fizz sits inside it

blocks.note: to test is to try out
Asti is the Italian sparkling wine

explanation.surface: Someone urging you to grab a bottle of fizz, since it is the best thing going.
explanation.walkthrough: Asti, from Piedmont in Italy, is the crossword's favourite sparkling wine; 'to get hold of' makes the trial word hold it.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of an adjective meaning full of flavour is an exact synonym for the finest to eat.

clue.text: A little chimp alarmed antelope

indicators.note: only a small part of the next two words is taken, running across the gap between them

blocks.note: the letters sit across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A small startled ape, or an animal startled by a chimp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A little' looks like it describes the chimp, but it tells you to take just a bit of 'chimp alarmed'.
explanation.definitionFit: The impala is a graceful African grazing animal, one species within the family of horned ruminants the definition names.

clue.text: Broadcaster’s escapade traps king in the Gherkin?

indicators.note: to trap is to hold inside, so the escapade encloses the royal abbreviation

blocks.note: Sky is the British satellite broadcaster, with its possessive S
a caper is an escapade
R is Rex, king

explanation.surface: A TV channel's prank that snares a monarch inside a famous London building.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gherkin is the nickname of the pickle-shaped tower at 30 St Mary Axe in the City of London; the question mark marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: That glass office tower is one instance of a very tall city building, so the definition works by example.

clue.text: Go pale following day in A&E

indicators.note: the abbreviation for day is placed inside the hospital department's letters

blocks.note: f is the abbreviation for following
the letters A and E, with the ampersand ignored
d is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: Turning white after a day spent waiting in a hospital emergency room.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E (Accident and Emergency) is the British hospital emergency department; here it just supplies the letters A and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Colour draining away from a face or fabric is to lose brightness, a verb synonym for whitening or becoming wan.

clue.text: Wager party accepts request for court activity

indicators.note: the wager takes in the request, holding it inside itself

blocks.note: a bet is a wager
an ask is a request
a ball is a formal party

explanation.surface: A gambling group granting permission for some legal proceedings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court activity' suggests lawyers; the court is a sports court. B(ASK)ET then BALL.
explanation.definitionFit: The hoop game is played indoors on a marked hardwood floor, so it is a sport done on that kind of playing area.

clue.text: Dad caught by one clenched hand – he won’t fight

blocks.note: pa = dad
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
I is the Roman numeral one
a fist is a clenched hand

explanation.surface: A father hit by someone's fist, yet refusing to strike back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught by' reads as a passive but is just C followed by the next pieces; in cricket scoring c means caught.
explanation.definitionFit: A person opposed to violence and war on principle refuses combat, which the phrase describes as a noun equivalent.

clue.text: Rouse OAP – he rebuilt La Scala, for one

indicators.note: rebuilding puts the same materials together again in a new form, so the letters are reassembled

blocks.note: ten letters of fodder, including the pensioner abbreviation

explanation.surface: Wake up the old-age pensioner: he is the builder who restored the famous Milan theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: OAP (old-age pensioner) is used purely as letters. La Scala is the great opera theatre in Milan.
explanation.definitionFit: The Milan theatre is a famous venue for staged musical drama, so it is one example of that kind of building.

clue.text: Energy company supporting composer, dropping American artist

indicators.note: in a down clue, a supporter sits underneath, so energy and company come after the composer
the composer lets go of the letter for American, losing it from his name

blocks.note: Edward Elgar, the English composer, before losing the A
A is the abbreviation for American; this is the letter removed
e is the physics symbol for energy
Co. is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A power firm sponsoring a composer, having dropped a US painter from the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Energy company' reads as one firm but is E plus CO, placed below ELGR in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek-born painter of Toledo is a celebrated Renaissance master, so he is one example of a painter.

clue.text: Knowing Mike isn’t involved in protest

indicators.note: the phonetic letter takes no part in the demonstration, so it is left out of that word

blocks.note: a march is a protest
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet; this letter goes

explanation.surface: Someone called Mike is conspicuously staying out of a demonstration.
explanation.walkthrough: Mike looks like a person's name, but it is the radio code for the letter M.
explanation.definitionFit: An arch look or remark is sly and playfully mischievous, an adjective synonym for a wry, sly manner.

clue.text: Surviving trace of rock band relative ultimately lost

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter of the next word is taken

blocks.note: R.E.M. is the American rock band
nan is a grandmother
the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Tracing a rock group's family member who has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' may suggest geology alongside 'trace', but it is the band R.E.M.
explanation.definitionFit: A small leftover piece of something otherwise gone is what the noun names, matching a remaining vestige.

clue.text: Tipsy cheerleader is concealing spirit

indicators.note: the two words before this phrase keep the answer tucked inside them

blocks.note: runs across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A drunk cheerleader secretly hiding a bottle of liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' teases alcohol after 'tipsy', but it means the soul.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek word for the soul or mind is used in English for someone's inner self, a synonym for that sense.

clue.text: No good drink for head

blocks.note: taken as it stands
g is the abbreviation for good
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: Advice that alcohol will do your brain no favours.
explanation.walkthrough: A noggin is also a small measure of drink, so 'drink' nearly defines the answer too; here the head is the slang sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal word for the skull or brain is slang for a person's top part, used in phrases like 'use your noggin'.

clue.text: I managed to grab somewhat masculine Dubliner

indicators.note: the phrase for 'I managed' seizes what follows, holding it inside

blocks.note: I + RAN, as in ran a business
-ish means somewhat
m is the abbreviation for masculine

explanation.surface: Someone boasting of snatching a rather manly man from Ireland's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somewhat masculine' reads as one description but is ISH plus M, both going inside I RAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident of Ireland's capital city is by nationality a man from that country, so the definition works by example.

clue.text: Regularly call up bishop’s team

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every other one from the following two words

blocks.note: the first, third and fifth letters of the two words run together
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A clergyman often phoning his side.
explanation.walkthrough: The alternate letters run across the space between 'call' and 'up'; the apostrophe-s in 'bishop's' is just surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A football side such as a Premier League outfit is called by this noun, a sporting synonym for an organised squad.

clue.text: Distinctive southern plaice swimming

indicators.note: a swimming fish moves about, so the letters of the flatfish move about too

blocks.note: s is the abbreviation for southern
the fish's letters, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A distinctive flatfish swimming in southern waters.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface fish is fitting: the anagram indicator is exactly what a plaice does.
explanation.definitionFit: Something marked out from the ordinary has its own character, so the adjectives are close synonyms for being unusual.

clue.text: Choose a former partner to return tool

indicators.note: coming back means travelling the other way, so the former partner's letters run backwards

blocks.note: to pick is to choose
taken as it stands
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: Deciding to ask an old flame to give back something borrowed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like relationship advice; 'return' here means turn round, not give back.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy digging implement with a pointed iron head is one example of a hand implement used by workers.

clue.text: Ref took bets about event in Munich

indicators.note: turned about means moved around, so the letters of the first four words are rearranged

blocks.note: eleven letters of fodder

explanation.surface: A corrupt referee taking wagers on a Bavarian festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning' but is the anagram indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: The annual beer festival held in the Bavarian capital each autumn is an example of a happening in that German city.
